sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: pedestrians, school zones, bicycles, motorcycles, large vehicles, buses and special vehicles
Audience: every first-time Oregon Class C applicant; sharing the road with pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists and buses is everyday driving law and heavy knowledge-test material.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the crosswalk turn rules differ by whether the intersection has a signal [A02], school speed signs apply at different times by sign type [A03], and the school bus stop rule depends on whether the median is unpaved or painted [A09].
Level: condition-and-action recall with several exact values (distances, school speed and hours, load overhang limits); moderate to heavy load.
Prerequisites: the turns and intersections section, especially yielding while turning and bike lanes, and the signs section, especially school and warning signs.

corpus_stability.reason: The Oregon Driver Manual is a two-year edition (the front cover names a two-year span and the back cover carries a single form revision code); fees and office details are sent to the DMV website rather than printed, and nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year.
